To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) continual common knowledge is a necessary and a sufficient condition for attaning EBA, and (2) given any EBA protocol, there is a simple two-step process that transforms it into a protocol that attains EBA using continual common knowledge.

(i) common knowledge of the nonfaulty processes is a necessary and a sufficient condition for attaning EBA in the crash failure mode, and (ii) common knowledge of all processes is a necessary condition for attaining E BA in the omission failure mode, and is a sufficient condition for the special case of EBA in which the processors are required to agree on the same value.
